reviewed_document.own_summary: The curriculum builds a text model from numbered characters, input/next-step answer pairs and a measurable guessing cost, then introduces trainable tables, context, attention and Transformer components. Chapters 5–7 make training, tokenization and dialogue positions explicit. Later branches study style/safety, images and sound, preferences, modern components, experts, measured efficiency, quantization and distillation. A/B/C add external retrieval, tools and extra computation. Chapter 19 integrates a deliberately small synthetic MoE; chapter 20 starts from an existing Dense vision-language model, builds candidate LoRA corrections, compares them against the unchanged base, and retains the base for this release. Whisper transcription then joins the same text/history/photo conversation input. Each route is a guide to concepts and examples rather than a promise that a short CPU example proves broad capability.

own_workflow_explanation.one_text_update: One sample is arranged into role-marked text, converted to IDs and split into input X and next-position target Y. A readable-history mask controls which preceding positions the model can use; answer scoring positions control which target errors count. Deliberate gradient accumulation uses a separately chosen clearing schedule.
own_workflow_explanation.preference_branch: Read 13.1–13.4 for same-question comparisons, answer probability and a fixed reference. DPO continues at 13.5–13.6; PPO starts with the scorer at 13.10 and follows 13.11–13.16. The chapter introduction now agrees with this split. The small PPO example selects whole prewritten answers, while the DPO examples score text answers.
own_workflow_explanation.natural_assistant: Try the selected product through 20.2 and the student guide; this needs no retraining. To study changes, prepare source-family splits, build a candidate correction, validate base plus both saved candidates, select using retention gates and the declared score, freeze that choice, and only then run the final test. Building a candidate does not commit the release to using it. Recorded audio is transcription/evaluation material, not a LoRA update to Whisper.
